p: Bradford was named the world's first UNESCO City of Film back in 2009, and once you know that, the National Science and Media Museum makes even more sense. The city has a rich history as a filming location, and its streets, mills and moors have turned up in countless films and TV dramas.

There's plenty more to explore in town. Little Germany, a short walk from the centre, is a quarter of grand Victorian warehouses built by wool merchants, many from Germany, and the architecture is seriously impressive. Cartwright Hall, in Lister Park, is an art gallery set in lovely parkland with a boating lake and Mughal-style water gardens. Bradford Industrial Museum, at Moorside Mills, tells the story of the city's textile past with working machinery.

Head a little further and the scenery opens up. Haworth, home of the Brontë sisters, is a short drive away, with its cobbled main street, the Brontë Parsonage Museum and wild moorland walks. The Keighley and Worth Valley Railway runs steam trains through the valley, and fans of The Railway Children will recognise Oakworth station.

For the museum itself, check what's showing in the cinemas while you plan your day, as an IMAX film or a classic screening can turn a good visit into a great one. Pack light, as there are lots of floors to cover, and use the lifts between levels if little legs are tired.
